candidate.educational_objective: Apply current USPSTF IPV guidance: screen women of reproductive age and connect positive screens with multicomponent ongoing support interventions.

options.A: Routine screening is recommended only when physical injuries are visible because asymptomatic women should not be screened.
options.B: Screen women of reproductive age, including pregnant and postpartum women, and provide or refer those who screen positive to evidence-based multicomponent interventions with ongoing support.
options.C: Screening is recommended only during pregnancy and not for nonpregnant women of reproductive age.
options.D: IPV screening is recommended only in emergency departments after an assault has already occurred.

candidate.rationale: The USPSTF 2025 Grade B recommendation calls for screening women of reproductive age, including pregnant and postpartum women, for IPV. The pathway to benefit includes providing or referring people who screen positive to evidence-based multicomponent interventions with ongoing support. B directly reflects the recommendation without making universal state-law reporting claims.
candidate.source_claim_supported: USPSTF recommends IPV screening for women of reproductive age, including pregnant/postpartum women, with referral/provision of multicomponent ongoing support for positive screens.
candidate.source_document_title: Intimate Partner Violence and Caregiver Abuse of Older or Vulnerable Adults: Screening

candidate.stem: During a routine primary-care visit, an asymptomatic 29-year-old woman is privately screened for intimate partner violence (IPV). Which statement best reflects current USPSTF guidance?
